To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the measured diversity gain of the LTE device is in accordance with the theoretical prediction of the model, and the measured MIMO gain is in accordance with theoretical prediction, and that the model is a simple and useful complement to measured results in evaluation and comparison of wireless devices.

a theoretical throughput model based on defining a threshold receiver for the LOS case, can be used to predict the throughput data rate for a MIMO LTE device with frequency diversity, both for the 1×2 SIMO case and the 2×2 MIMO case.

we have presented a simple theoretical model of the throughput data rate in a MIMO OFDM system under frequency selective fading, and that this model is in good agreement with measurements in reverberation chamber.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods to improve the accuracy and efficiency in the characterization of electromagnetic (EM) environments.
the performance of wireless devices in the presence of fading, multipath, interference and noise.
the performance of wireless devices in a reverberating environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple model based on an ideal threshold receiver can be used to describe the throughput of a commercial LTE receiver in reverberation chamber measurements.

the measured throughput data rate of the LTE device is in agreement with the theoretical model, and the model can therefore be used as a reference for the performance of LTE devices under frequency selective fading in the reverberation chamber.
the throughput model and measured results in reverberation chambers can be used to complement each other in evaluation of performance in realistic scenarios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the model can be used to complement the measured results, but that the model is not a substitute for measurements, since there is a need to include more details on the receiver, e.g., on the coding and modulation schemes.
we have shown how a simple theoretical model can be used to explain the performance of a commercial LTE terminal in a reverberating environment.
a simple theoretical throughput model for a wireless device can be used to complement measurements in a reverboration chamber.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the throughput of a wireless device with MIMO and frequency diversity can be accurately predicted using a simple threshold receiver model.
the diversity gain from MIMO and OFDM is very similar for the measured case.

the theoretical throughput model can be used to complement measurements in reverberation chambers to obtain the throughput data rate for a given device in the presence of frequency selective fading, which can be used in evaluation of performance.
